oid.description: OID is the numeric object identifier, for example 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0.

type.description:
Type is the SNMP value type, for example STRING, INTEGER, OID,
Counter32, Gauge32 or Hex-STRING.

value.description: Value is the value served for the OID, interpreted per `type`.

AddMib.description: AddMib represents a MIB override or addition.

device.description: Device is the `name` of the device carrying the interface.

interface.description:
Interface is the interface `name` on that device, as declared in its
`interfaces` list.

type.description:
Type is the fault to inject. Interface-scoped only: these raise SNMP
counters, they do not take a service (DHCP, DNS) out.

value.description: Value is the rate or percentage, 1..100, applied while the phase runs.

BehaviorFault.description: BehaviorFault sets one supported SNMP interface fault rate.

name.description: Name identifies the phase in the runtime view.

start_offset_ms.description:
StartOffsetMS is when this phase begins, measured from the start of the
timeline (not from the previous phase).

duration_ms.description: DurationMS is how long the phase's traffic and faults stay applied.

reset.description:
Reset clears the traffic and faults set by earlier phases before this
one applies its own, instead of layering on top of them.

traffic.description: Traffic sets observable interface utilization for the phase's duration.

faults.description: Faults injects SNMP-visible interface faults for the phase's duration.

BehaviorPhase.description: BehaviorPhase applies traffic and faults at a deterministic offset.

name.description:
Name identifies the timeline in the runtime view and the API. Unique
within the config.

start_offset_ms.description:
StartOffsetMS delays the whole timeline this many milliseconds after
the session starts. 0 starts it immediately.

repeat_count.description:
RepeatCount is how many times the phase sequence runs, 1..1000. There
is no infinite repeat; pick a count that covers the intended run.

phases.description:
Phases are the ordered steps of the timeline. Each phase's
start_offset_ms is relative to the timeline, not to the previous phase.

BehaviorTimeline.description: BehaviorTimeline is one saved, repeatable sequence of runtime phases.

device.description: Device is the `name` of the device carrying the interface.

interface.description:
Interface is the interface `name` on that device, as declared in its
`interfaces` list.

utilization.description:
Utilization is the percentage, 1..100, reported through the interface's
IF-MIB counters while the phase is active.

BehaviorTraffic.description: BehaviorTraffic sets observable utilization on one simulated interface.

file_name.description:
FileName is the pcap or pcapng file to replay, resolved against
`include_path` when relative.

loop_time.description:
LoopTime is the seconds to wait before replaying the file again.
0 replays it once.

scale_time.description:
ScaleTime multiplies the capture's inter-packet gaps: 2.0 replays at
half speed, 0.5 at double. Omit or 0 replays at the recorded rate.

enabled.description:
Enabled advertises CDP from this device, overriding the fleet-wide
`discovery_protocols.cdp`.

advertise_interval.description: AdvertiseInterval is the seconds between advertisements. Omit for 60.

holdtime.description: Holdtime is the seconds a neighbour should hold this advertisement.

version.description: Version is the CDP protocol version advertised, 1 or 2.

software_version.description: SoftwareVersion is the advertised software version string.

platform.description:
Platform is the advertised platform string, for example
"cisco WS-C3750X-48P".

port_id.description: PortID is the advertised port identifier.

CdpConfig.description: CdpConfig represents CDP discovery protocol configuration.

community.description: Community is the community string that selects this walk.

walk_file.description: WalkFile is the walk served to pollers using that community.

CommunityInclude.description: CommunityInclude represents a community-specific walk include.

include_path.description:
IncludePath is a directory the loader searches for files referenced by
relative path elsewhere in this config (walk files, capture files).
Relative to the config file's own directory when itself relative.

capture_playbacks.description:
CapturePlaybacks replays a recorded PCAP alongside the simulated
devices. At most one entry: the runtime plays exactly one capture
(config.Config.CapturePlayback, one engine in the replay controller).
The schema kept the shape of a list, so extra entries were dropped on
load and deleted from disk on the next save. Refuse them instead.

behavior_timelines.description:
BehaviorTimelines are saved, repeatable sequences of runtime phases
that drive traffic and faults on a schedule after the session starts.
Up to 64 timelines; they run concurrently.

discovery_protocols.description:
DiscoveryProtocols sets the fleet-wide default for LLDP, CDP, EDP and
FDP advertisement. A device's own lldp/cdp/edp/fdp block overrides it.

devices.description:
Devices is the simulated device set served as a single untagged
segment. Mutually exclusive with `segments`: when segments is present,
this must be empty.

segments.description:
Segments binds independent device sets to VLAN tags for multi-VLAN
playback (ADR 0008). When present, each segment is served as its own
isolated network (own IP space) on its tag, and top-level `devices` must
be empty. When absent, `devices` is served as a single untagged segment —
today's flat behavior.

networks.description:
Networks declares the routed IPv4 networks devices attach to. An
interface naming one in its `network` field must carry an `address`
written as a prefix (10.10.0.5/24), not a bare address.

attachments.description:
Attachments bind this config's virtual networks to the deployment's
host-side interfaces. Preflight rejects an attachment naming a network
this config does not declare, or a host interface the daemon's
attachment policy does not permit.

Config.description: Config represents the YAML configuration structure.

name.description: Name is the hostname, for example clinic-rtr-01.clinic.local.

ip.description:
IP is the record's address. The key is `ip`, not `address` — an
`address` key is rejected by the strict loader.

ttl.description: TTL is the record's time to live in seconds.

rcode.description:
RCode answers this record with a DNS response code instead of the
address, 0..15 — 3 is NXDOMAIN, which is how a lookup failure is
authored.

DNSRecord.description: DNSRecord represents a DNS A or PTR record.

forward_records.description: ForwardRecords are name-to-address (A) records this server answers.

reverse_records.description: ReverseRecords are address-to-name (PTR) records this server answers.

name.description:
Name is the device's identity across the config: behaviour phases,
trunk_ports.remote_device and the topology graph all refer to it.
Unique within the config, and read-only once the device exists — the
daemon takes a device's name from the URL, so renaming through the
editor is not supported.

type.description:
Type selects the device persona: which MIBs it serves, which icon the
topology draws and how a scanner classifies it. Note the authored
spelling: the vocabulary hyphenates, so `voip-phone` and
`layer3-switch` are accepted and their underscored forms are not. An
access point is `ap` or `access-point`, never `access_point`.

mac.description:
MAC is the device's explicit base MAC address (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff).
Mutually exclusive with `vendor`: set one or the other, never both.

vendor.description:
Vendor derives the MAC from a vendor OUI instead of stating one.
Mutually exclusive with `mac`. Set `mac_suffix` alongside it: without a
suffix every device of the same vendor collides on the same address,
ending :00:00:00.

mac_suffix.description:
MACSuffix is the per-device low 24 bits appended to the vendor OUI,
0..16777215. Required in practice whenever `vendor` is used more than
once.

ips.description:
IPs are the device's addresses as bare IPs (10.10.0.5), used when the
device is not modelled through `interfaces` and `networks`. Interface
addresses use a prefix instead.

vlan.description:
VLAN is the access VLAN, 1..4094, for a device served on a trunk
without its own interface list.

map_to_ip.description:
MapToIP answers for this additional address as well, so one simulated
device can respond on a second IP.

babble.description:
Babble makes the device emit unsolicited background chatter, so a
passive scanner sees it without probing.

ttl.description:
TTL configures ICMP TTL expiry so the device appears as a traceroute
hop. It is an object (ttl / ip / mask), not a bare integer — a plain
`ttl: 64` is rejected. The per-packet IP TTL lives in
`os_fingerprint.ttl`.

snmp_agent.description:
SnmpAgent serves SNMP for this device, from a walk file and/or
individual OID overrides.

dhcp.description:
Dhcp makes the device a DHCP server. Its pool must sit inside a routed
network this config declares, or preflight rejects the config.

dns.description:
DNS makes the device a DNS server. Its records key the address as `ip`,
not `address`.

lldp.description:
Lldp overrides the fleet-wide `discovery_protocols.lldp` for this
device and carries its advertised strings.

cdp.description: Cdp overrides the fleet-wide `discovery_protocols.cdp` for this device.

edp.description: Edp overrides the fleet-wide `discovery_protocols.edp` for this device.

fdp.description: Fdp overrides the fleet-wide `discovery_protocols.fdp` for this device.

stp.description:
Stp makes the device participate in spanning tree, so a scanner sees
bridge priorities and a root election.

http.description:
HTTP serves a web listener with author-defined endpoints, which is what
makes a device identifiable as a server or an appliance.

ftp.description: Ftp serves an FTP listener with a banner and optional accounts.

netbios.description:
Netbios answers NetBIOS name queries, which is how Windows-facing
scanners name a host. Names are capped at 15 characters.

mdns.description:
Mdns publishes the device and its services over multicast DNS, the way
Bonjour and Avahi announce a printer or a camera.

snmpv3.description:
Snmpv3 adds USM users for authenticated, optionally encrypted SNMP.
Independent of `snmp_agent`, which serves v1/v2c.

icmp.description: Icmp configures ping and IPv4 router advertisement behaviour.

icmpv6.description:
Icmpv6 configures IPv6 ping, neighbour discovery and router
advertisement behaviour.

dhcpv6.description:
Dhcpv6 makes the device a DHCPv6 server. Omit the block entirely when
the device should not serve DHCPv6: an empty `dhcpv6: {}` is a
configured server that picks up the default lifetimes.

os_fingerprint.description:
OSFingerprint shapes the device's TCP/IP stack and service banners so a
fingerprinting scanner identifies the intended operating system.

ssh.description:
SSH serves an authenticated vendor-like CLI. The password is never
written in the config: `password_env` names an environment variable
that must be set in the daemon's environment, or the device cannot
start.

syslog.description:
Syslog sends this device's state-change messages to RFC 5424
collectors.

iperf3.description: IPerf3 answers iperf3 throughput tests with the authored rates.

reflector.description:
Reflector makes the device a NetAlly-style UDP reflector endpoint for
TrueSpeed and performance tests. Presence enables it; there is no
separate enable flag.

interfaces.description:
Interfaces declares the device's ports: addresses, speeds, status and
the network each one attaches to. This is what IF-MIB reports and what
behaviour phases target by name.

routes.description: Routes are static IPv4 routes this device advertises and forwards on.

trunk_ports.description:
TrunkPorts declare the VLAN-tagged links to neighbouring devices. This
is how topology edges are authored — there is no separate `links`
section; an edge exists because a trunk port names a `remote_device`.

port_channels.description:
PortChannels bundle member interfaces into a LAG. They draw no edge on
their own: a trunk_port whose `interface` is "port-channel<id>" is what
surfaces the link.

properties.description:
Properties is a free-form vendor-metadata block used by the
vendor template pack (cmd/niac/templates/vendor-templates) to
carry vendor / model / OS / port-config strings into the
device list. Keys are author-defined; consumers treat unknown
keys as informational. The loader's own derived keys (vlan,
custom_mibs_count) are not authored here.

client_ip.description: ClientIP is the address reserved for the matching client.

mac_addr_value.description: MacAddrValue is the client MAC the reservation matches.

mac_addr_mask.description:
MacAddrMask masks MacAddrValue so a reservation can match a range of
MACs, such as a whole vendor OUI.

DhcpLease.description: DhcpLease represents a DHCP client lease.

client_leases.description: ClientLeases are fixed reservations handed to matching clients.

subnet_mask.description: SubnetMask is option 1, the mask offered to clients.

router.description: Router is option 3, the default gateway offered to clients.

domain_name_server.description: DomainNameServer is option 6, the DNS server offered to clients.

next_server_ip.description:
NextServerIP is the siaddr field, the TFTP server a booting client
should fetch its image from.

server_identifier.description: ServerIdentifier is option 54, this server's own address.

pool_start.description:
PoolStart is the first address of the dynamic pool. The pool must sit
inside a routed network this config declares, or preflight rejects it.

pool_end.description: PoolEnd is the last address of the dynamic pool.

ntp_servers.description: NTPServers is option 42, the NTP servers offered to clients.

domain_search.description: DomainSearch is option 119, the domain search list.

tftp_server_name.description: TFTPServerName is option 66, the boot server name.

bootfile_name.description: BootfileName is option 67, the boot file a client should request.

vendor_specific.description:
VendorSpecific is option 43, vendor-specific information as a hex
string.

sntp_servers_v6.description: SNTPServersV6 is DHCPv6 option 31, the SNTP servers offered.

ntp_servers_v6.description: NTPServersV6 is DHCPv6 option 56, the NTP servers offered.

sip_servers_v6.description: SIPServersV6 is DHCPv6 option 22, the SIP servers offered.

sip_domains_v6.description: SIPDomainsV6 is DHCPv6 option 21, the SIP domain list offered.

enabled.description: Enabled serves DHCPv6.

pools.description: Pools are the IPv6 address ranges handed out.

preferred_lifetime.description: PreferredLifetime is the seconds a lease stays preferred.

valid_lifetime.description: ValidLifetime is the seconds a lease stays valid.

preference.description:
Preference is the server preference, 0..255; a client prefers the
highest.

dns_servers.description: DNSServers are the DNS servers offered to clients.

domain_list.description: DomainList is the domain search list offered to clients.

sntp_servers.description: SNTPServers are the SNTP servers offered to clients.

ntp_servers.description: NTPServers are the NTP servers offered to clients.

sip_servers.description: SIPServers are the SIP servers offered to clients.

sip_domains.description: SIPDomains is the SIP domain list offered to clients.

network.description: Network is the pool's prefix, for example 2001:db8:1::/64.

range_start.description: RangeStart is the first address handed out.

range_end.description: RangeEnd is the last address handed out.

Dhcpv6Pool.description: Dhcpv6Pool represents an IPv6 address pool.

lldp.description: LLDP sets the fleet-wide default for IEEE 802.1AB advertisement.

cdp.description: CDP sets the fleet-wide default for Cisco Discovery Protocol.

edp.description: EDP sets the fleet-wide default for Extreme Discovery Protocol.

fdp.description: FDP sets the fleet-wide default for Foundry Discovery Protocol.

enabled.description: Enabled advertises EDP (Extreme) from this device.

advertise_interval.description: AdvertiseInterval is the seconds between advertisements.

version_string.description: VersionString is the advertised software version.

display_string.description: DisplayString is the advertised system display name.

EdpConfig.description: EdpConfig represents EDP discovery protocol configuration.

port.description: Port is the bridge port number the entry is learned on.

vlan.description: VLAN is the VLAN id the entry belongs to.

FdbTableConfig.description: FdbTableConfig configures SNMP forwarding database table injection.

enabled.description: Enabled advertises FDP (Foundry) from this device.

advertise_interval.description: AdvertiseInterval is the seconds between advertisements.

holdtime.description: Holdtime is the seconds a neighbour should hold this advertisement.

software_version.description: SoftwareVersion is the advertised software version string.

platform.description: Platform is the advertised platform string.

port_id.description: PortID is the advertised port identifier.

FdpConfig.description: FdpConfig represents FDP discovery protocol configuration.

enabled.description: Enabled serves the FTP listener.

welcome_banner.description: WelcomeBanner is the 220 greeting, a primary identification signal.

system_type.description: SystemType is the SYST response, for example "UNIX Type: L8".

allow_anonymous.description: AllowAnonymous accepts the anonymous account without a password.

users.description: Users are the accounts the server accepts.

password.description:
Password is the account password. Unlike SSH, this is written in the
config — use only simulated credentials, never a real one.

home_dir.description: HomeDir is the directory the account lands in.

FtpUser.description: FtpUser represents an FTP user account.

enabled.description: Enabled serves the HTTP listener.

server_name.description:
ServerName is the Server response header, a signal a scanner uses to
identify the platform.

endpoints.description:
Endpoints are the paths this server answers. A request to any other
path gets 404.

path.description: Path is the request path, for example /status.

method.description: Method is the HTTP method matched. Omit for GET.

status_code.description: StatusCode is the response status. Omit for 200.

content_type.description: ContentType is the response Content-Type header.

body.description: Body is the response body served verbatim.

HTTPEndpoint.description: HTTPEndpoint represents an HTTP endpoint configuration.

enabled.description: Enabled serves the iperf3 listener.

port.description: Port is the TCP port iperf3 listens on. Omit for the default, 5201.

max_bandwidth_mbps.description: MaxBandwidthMbps caps the throughput the device will report.

typical_latency_ms.description: TypicalLatencyMs is the round-trip latency reported to the tester.

jitter_ms.description: JitterMs is the variation reported around the typical latency.

packet_loss_percent.description: PacketLossPercent is the loss rate reported to the tester, 0..100.

upload_mbps.description: UploadMbps is the reported client-to-server rate.

download_mbps.description: DownloadMbps is the reported server-to-client rate.

IPerf3Config.description: IPerf3Config represents iPerf3 server emulation configuration.

enabled.description:
Enabled answers ICMP echo requests, which is what makes the device
pingable.

ttl.description: TTL is the TTL stamped on ICMP replies.

rate_limit.description: RateLimit caps replies per second; further requests are dropped.

address_mask_reply.description: AddressMaskReply is the mask answered to an ICMP address mask request.

router_advertisement.description: RouterAdvertisement makes the device announce itself as an IPv4 router.

address.description: Address is the advertised router's IPv4 address.

preference.description: Preference is the advertised preference level; higher wins.

IcmpRouter.description: IcmpRouter represents an advertised router entry.

period.description: Period is the seconds between advertisements.

lifetime.description: Lifetime is the seconds a client should consider the router valid.

routers.description: Routers are the advertised router entries.

enabled.description: Enabled answers ICMPv6 echo and neighbour solicitation.

hop_limit.description: HopLimit is the hop limit stamped on ICMPv6 replies.

router_advertisement.description: RouterAdvertisement makes the device announce itself as an IPv6 router.

prefix_length.description: PrefixLength is the advertised prefix length, typically 64.

onlink.description: Onlink sets the L flag: the prefix is on-link.

auto.description: Auto sets the A flag: clients may autoconfigure from this prefix.

valid_lifetime.description: ValidLifetime is the seconds the prefix stays valid.

preferred_lifetime.description: PreferredLifetime is the seconds the prefix stays preferred.

prefix.description: Prefix is the advertised IPv6 prefix, for example 2001:db8:1::.

Icmpv6PrefixInfo.description: Icmpv6PrefixInfo represents IPv6 prefix info options.

period.description: Period is the seconds between advertisements.

cur_hop_limit.description: CurHopLimit is the hop limit clients should adopt.

managed.description: Managed sets the M flag: clients should use DHCPv6 for addresses.

other.description:
Other sets the O flag: clients should use DHCPv6 for other
configuration only.

lifetime.description: Lifetime is the seconds this router stays a valid default.

reachable_time.description: ReachableTime is the milliseconds a neighbour is assumed reachable.

retrans_timer.description: RetransTimer is the milliseconds between neighbour solicitations.

mtu.description: MTU is the link MTU advertised to clients.

prefix_info.description: PrefixInfo are the advertised prefixes clients autoconfigure from.

name.description:
Name is the port name, for example GigabitEthernet0/1 or eth0.
Behaviour phases and trunk ports target the interface by this name.

type.description: Type is the IF-MIB interface type reported for this port.

network.description:
Network is the `networks[].name` this port attaches to. When set, the
port's `address` must be written as a prefix and must fall inside that
network's subnet.

address.description:
Address is the port's IPv4 address, written as a prefix
(10.10.0.5/24) — a bare address is rejected. When `network` is set the
address must fall inside that network's subnet and carry the same
prefix length; a /32 host address on a /24 network is refused.

mtu.description: MTU is the port's MTU in bytes, 576..1000000.

speed.description: Speed is the port's nominal speed in Mbps, reported through IF-MIB.

duplex.description: Duplex is the port's duplex mode.

admin_status.description: AdminStatus is the configured state of the port (ifAdminStatus).

oper_status.description:
OperStatus is the observed state of the port (ifOperStatus). A link
fault drives this down at runtime.

description.description: Description is the port's ifAlias text, as a switch's port description.

in_utilization.description:
InUtilization is the steady-state inbound utilization percentage,
0..100, before any behaviour phase changes it.

out_utilization.description:
OutUtilization is the steady-state outbound utilization percentage,
0..100, before any behaviour phase changes it.

vlans.description: VLANs are the VLAN ids carried on this port when it is a switch port.

Interface.description: Interface represents configured metadata for a device interface.

enabled.description: Enabled arms link-state traps.

link_down.description: LinkDown sends a trap when an interface goes down.

link_up.description: LinkUp sends a trap when an interface comes up.

enabled.description:
Enabled advertises LLDP from this device, overriding the fleet-wide
`discovery_protocols.lldp`.

advertise_interval.description: AdvertiseInterval is the seconds between advertisements. Omit for 30.

ttl.description: TTL is the seconds a neighbour should hold this advertisement.

system_description.description: SystemDescription is the advertised system description TLV.

port_description.description: PortDescription is the advertised port description TLV.

chassis_id_type.description:
ChassisIDType selects which chassis ID subtype is advertised, for
example mac or local.

LldpConfig.description: LldpConfig represents LLDP discovery protocol configuration.

name.description:
Name labels this attachment. It is what a session's binding selects the
attachment by at start time, not a network name — a binding naming an
attachment this config does not declare is reported as
`unknown_attachment`.

connect.description:
Connect is the `networks[].name` this attachment exposes to the host.
Whether the host interface may actually carry it is decided at start
against the daemon's attachment policy, which reports
`attachment_policy_denied` or `host_interface_unavailable`;
`niac validate` has no host binding and cannot check those.

LogicalAttachment.description: LogicalAttachment names the virtual network exposed by a deployment binding.

enabled.description: Enabled publishes this device over mDNS.

hostname.description: Hostname is the advertised name, without the .local suffix.

services.description:
Services are the DNS-SD services advertised, which is what makes a
printer or a camera discoverable as such.

ttl.description: TTL is the seconds a resolver should cache these records.

MdnsConfig.description: MdnsConfig publishes a device on multicast DNS, the way Bonjour and Avahi announce a host and its services on the local link.

type.description: Type is the DNS-SD service type, for example _ipp._tcp or _rtsp._tcp.

port.description: Port is the TCP or UDP port the service is advertised on.

txt.description: TXT are the service's TXT record key=value strings.

MdnsService.description: MdnsService is one advertised DNS-SD service, such as _ipp._tcp.

enabled.description: Enabled answers NetBIOS name queries.

name.description:
Name is the NetBIOS name, at most 15 characters — longer names are
truncated on the wire, so authored names should already be short.

workgroup.description: Workgroup is the advertised workgroup or domain.

node_type.description: NodeType is the NetBIOS node type, for example B, P, M or H.

services.description: Services are the advertised service suffixes.

ttl.description: TTL is the seconds a resolver should cache the name.

names.description: Names are additional NetBIOS name entries served by this device.

msbrowse.description:
MsBrowse advertises the __MSBROWSE__ entry, marking the device as a
master browser.

name.description: Name is the entry's NetBIOS name, at most 15 characters.

suffix.description:
Suffix is the two-hex-digit name suffix, for example 00 (workstation)
or 20 (file server).

group.description: Group marks the entry as a group name rather than a unique name.

NetbiosName.description: NetbiosName represents a NetBIOS name entry.

name.description:
Name is how interfaces and attachments refer to this network. Unique
within the config.

subnet.description:
Subnet is the network in CIDR form, for example 10.10.0.0/24. Every
interface address on this network must fall inside it, and a DHCP pool
served onto it must sit within the same subnet.

virtual_vlan.description:
VirtualVLAN tags this network's frames with a VLAN id, 1..4094, when
the network is served on a trunk. Omit for untagged.

Network.description: Network declares one internal routed IPv4 network.

os_type.description:
OSType is the operating system to imitate, for example "linux",
"windows", "cisco-ios" or "juniper-junos".

ttl.description:
TTL is the default IP TTL stamped on outbound packets, which is a
primary fingerprinting signal (Linux 64, Windows 128, Cisco 255).

window_size.description: WindowSize is the advertised TCP window size.

window_scale.description: WindowScale is the TCP window scale option.

mss.description: MSS is the TCP maximum segment size.

ssh_banner.description: SSHBanner is the SSH version banner presented on connect.

http_server.description: HTTPServer is the HTTP Server response header.

ftp_banner.description: FTPBanner is the FTP welcome banner.

smtp_banner.description: SMTPBanner is the SMTP greeting banner.

telnet_banner.description: TelnetBanner is the Telnet greeting banner.

dont_fragment.description:
DontFragment sets the IP DF bit, another fingerprinting signal
(typically true on Linux, false on Windows).

OSFingerprintConfig.description: OSFingerprintConfig represents OS fingerprinting configuration for device simulation.

id.description:
ID is the channel number; a trunk port refers to the bundle as
"port-channel<id>".

members.description: Members are the `interfaces[].name` values bundled into the channel.

mode.description: Mode is the LACP mode, for example active, passive or on.

PortChannel.description: PortChannel declares a Link Aggregation (LACP) bundle.

enabled.description:
Enabled turns the protocol on for every device that does not override
it with its own block.

interval.description:
Interval is the advertisement interval in seconds. Omit for the
protocol's own default (30 s for LLDP, 60 s for CDP).

latency_ms.description:
LatencyMs delays the reflected packet by this many milliseconds,
simulating one-way path latency (Java Latency()). 0 = reflect
immediately.

jitter_ms.description:
JitterMs randomises the delay by +/- this many milliseconds around
LatencyMs (Java Jitter()). 0 = no jitter.

dscp.description:
DSCP selects which ToS bits are toggled on the reflected packet:
true wiggles the bottom two DSCP bits (0x03, Java Dscp), false
wiggles the IP-precedence bit (0x01, Java IpPrecedence — the default).

ReflectorConfig.description: ReflectorConfig represents a NetAlly-style UDP reflector endpoint.

destination.description:
Destination is the target network in CIDR form, for example
10.20.0.0/24. Use 0.0.0.0/0 for a default route.

via.description: Via is the `name` of the local interface the route leaves by.

next_hop.description: NextHop is the gateway's bare IPv4 address — an address, not a prefix.

Route.description: Route declares an IPv4 static route through a named device interface.

enabled.description:
Enabled serves the SSH listener. When true, username and password_env
are both required.

username.description: Username is the account the simulated CLI accepts.

password_env.description:
PasswordEnv names the environment variable holding the password — the
password itself is never written in the config. That variable must be
set in the daemon's environment or the device fails to start.

SSHConfig.description: SSHConfig enables authenticated vendor-like command sessions.

tag.description: Tag is "untagged" (the native VLAN) or a VLAN id in 1..4094.

devices.description: Devices is an inline device set for this segment.

config.description:
Config is a path to a config file whose devices form this segment
(resolved by the loader). Mutually exclusive with Devices.

Segment.description: Segment binds a device set to a VLAN tag for multi-VLAN playback.

enabled.description:
Enabled serves SNMP for this device. Omit to inherit the default,
which is enabled whenever the block is present.

community.description: Community is the v1/v2c read community string. Omit for "public".

sysname.description:
SysName is sysName.0, the device's SNMP name. It overrides whatever the
walk file carries.

sysdescr.description:
SysDescr is sysDescr.0, the description string a scanner reads to
identify the platform and OS version.

syscontact.description:
SysContact is sysContact.0. Starter walks carry a placeholder here;
keep real customer contacts out of shipped content.

syslocation.description:
SysLocation is sysLocation.0. Starter walks carry a placeholder here;
keep real customer locations out of shipped content.

walk_file.description:
WalkFile is the recorded SNMP walk this device replays, resolved
against `include_path` when relative. It supplies every OID not
overridden by the fields above or by `add_mibs`.

walk_files.description: WalkFiles is several walk files merged in order, later entries winning.

add_mibs.description: AddMibs sets or overrides individual OIDs on top of the walk.

community_includes.description:
CommunityIncludes serve a different walk file per community string, so
one device can answer differently to different pollers.

access_list.description: AccessList restricts which source addresses may poll this agent.

snmp_addr.description:
SnmpAddr binds the agent to a specific address when the device has
more than one.

dot1d_fdb_table.description:
Dot1DFdbTable injects a bridge forwarding-database entry, so a scanner
walking dot1dTpFdbTable sees this device's neighbours.

dot1q_fdb_table.description:
Dot1QFdbTable injects a VLAN-aware forwarding-database entry
(dot1qTpFdbTable).

traps.description:
Traps sends SNMP notifications to receivers on cold start and on link
state changes.

enabled.description:
Enabled answers SNMPv3 requests. Independent of `snmp_agent`, which
serves v1/v2c.

engine_id.description:
EngineID is the USM engine identifier as a hex string. Omit to derive
one from the device's MAC.

users.description: Users are the USM accounts this agent accepts.

Snmpv3Config.description: Snmpv3Config represents SNMPv3 user / auth / priv configuration.

username.description: Username is the USM security name.

auth_protocol.description: AuthProtocol is the authentication digest. "none" is noAuthNoPriv.

auth_password.description:
AuthPassword is the authentication passphrase, at least 8 characters.
Simulated credentials only.

priv_protocol.description:
PrivProtocol is the privacy cipher. Requires an auth protocol —
there is no privNoAuth mode in USM.

priv_password.description:
PrivPassword is the privacy passphrase, at least 8 characters.
Simulated credentials only.

Snmpv3User.description: Snmpv3User represents one SNMPv3 USM user record.

enabled.description: Enabled makes the device participate in spanning tree.

bridge_priority.description:
BridgePriority is the bridge priority; the lowest value in the segment
wins the root election. Multiples of 4096.

hello_time.description: HelloTime is the seconds between BPDUs.

max_age.description: MaxAge is the seconds a BPDU stays valid.

forward_delay.description: ForwardDelay is the seconds a port spends in listening and learning.

version.description:
Version selects the spanning-tree flavour, for example stp, rstp
or mstp.

enabled.description:
Enabled turns on syslog emission for this device. When true, at least
one receiver is required.

receivers.description:
Receivers are collector endpoints as "host:port", for example
10.10.0.9:514.

SyslogConfig.description: SyslogConfig sends configuration-state messages to RFC 5424 collectors.

ttl.description:
TTL is the hop count at which this device answers with ICMP time
exceeded, placing it at that position in a traceroute.

ip.description: IP is the source address the time-exceeded message comes from.

mask.description: Mask is the netmask paired with IP when the hop answers for a range.

TTLConfig.description: TTLConfig configures ICMP TTL timeout behavior (traceroute simulation).

enabled.description: Enabled arms this trigger.

on_startup.description: OnStartup fires the trap once when the session starts.

TrapTriggerConfig.description: TrapTriggerConfig configures a simple trap trigger.

enabled.description: Enabled sends SNMP notifications from this device.

receivers.description:
Receivers are trap destinations as "host:port", conventionally port
162.

community.description: Community is the community string sent with v2c traps.

cold_start.description: ColdStart sends a coldStart trap when the device comes up.

link_state.description:
LinkState sends linkUp and linkDown traps as interfaces change, which
is how an injected link fault reaches an NMS.

interface.description:
Interface is the local port carrying the trunk, matching an
`interfaces[].name`, or "port-channel<id>" for a LAG.

vlans.description:
VLANs are the tagged VLAN ids the trunk carries. A port with no VLANs
and no native VLAN is an access port, not a trunk.

native_vlan.description: NativeVLAN is the untagged VLAN on this trunk.

remote_device.description:
RemoteDevice is the `name` of the device at the far end. This is what
draws the topology edge; without it the port is a stub.

remote_interface.description: RemoteInterface is the far-end port name, used to label the edge.

fdb_only.description:
FDBOnly records the neighbour in the forwarding database without
drawing a topology edge, for a device seen but not linked.

TrunkPort.description: TrunkPort declares a VLAN-tagged trunk link to a neighbouring device.

title: NIAC configuration
description: Network In A Can simulation configuration. Generated from the Go struct internal/converter.Config; refresh with `make schema` after struct changes.
